index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure illustrates a VNN-based pipeline for predicting Δ-Age, which represents the difference between estimated brain age and chronological age. The global layout is a left-to-right flowchart, starting with two input data sources on the left: an anatomical covariance matrix of size m₁ × m₁, visualized as a blue-to-yellow heatmap with axes labeled from 0 to m₁, and cortical thickness data comprising m₁ features, represented by a purple 3D brain model. Both inputs feed into a central 'VNN model' block, depicted as a rounded rectangle with a dark blue border and white fill. From this model, two pathways diverge: a solid black arrow leads to a 'Readout (unweighted mean)' block, shown as a yellow rectangle, which then connects via another solid arrow to a 'Brain age estimation' block, also yellow. This estimation step feeds into a final analysis box, outlined with a thick black border, containing two components: a 3D brain illustration with red regions indicating areas relevant to Δ-Age, and a boxplot labeled 'Δ-Age' comparing healthy (green) and pathology (red) groups. Simultaneously, a dashed black arrow from the VNN model points downward to a light green rectangular block labeled 'Regional analysis of final layer outputs', which in turn connects via a dashed arrow to the same final analysis box, linking the regional output analysis to the visualization of Δ-Age-relevant brain regions and the comparative boxplot. The figure uses color coding consistently: yellow for processing steps after the VNN, green for healthy group data, red for pathology, and blue for the covariance matrix. All text labels are in black sans-serif font, and the overall structure emphasizes a dual-path workflow—mainstream brain age estimation and parallel regional interpretability analysis—converging on the final Δ-Age assessment.
